questions.knowledge_point: Finding a Vector Given Its Coordinates Relative To a Given Basis
questions.problem:
Find the vector $x$, if $B={{b}_{1},{b}_{2}}$ is a basis of $\text{Span}{{b}_{1},{b}_{2}},$ and 

$$
{b}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0 \\ -5\end{aligned}],\,{b}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 7\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
We know that any vector in  $\text{Span}{{b}_{1},{b}_{2}}$ has the form

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0 \\ -5\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

 

where ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ are the coordinates relative to the basis $\,B.$ Since we are told that $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 7\end{aligned}],$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={{(\,3\,)}_{⏟}}_{{x}_{1}}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0 \\ -5\end{aligned}]+{{(\,7\,)}_{⏟}}_{{x}_{2}}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]= \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 0 \\ -15\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}14 \\ -14 \\ 14\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}11 \\ -14 \\ -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Coordinates of a Vector Relative To a Given Basis by Inspection
questions.problem:
Find the coordinates of the vector $x$ relative to the basis $B={{b}_{1},{b}_{2}},$ where

$$
{b}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{b}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -6\end{aligned}].
$$

If $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]$ then what is the value of ${x}_{1}?$
questions.worked_solution:
Remember, the order of the vectors in a basis is important.

Notice that 

$$
{{[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -6\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}={{(\,-6\,)}_{⏟}}_{{x}_{1}}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{b}_{1}}+{{(\,4\,)}_{⏟}}_{{x}_{2}}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{b}_{2}}
$$

which means that

$$
x=(-6)\cdot {b}_{1}+4\cdot {b}_{2}
$$

and therefore

$$
[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}-6 \\ 4\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, we have that ${x}_{1}=-6.$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Coordinates of a Vector Relative To a Given Basis Containing Two Vectors
questions.problem:
Find the coordinates of the vector $x$ relative to the basis $B={{b}_{1},{b}_{2}},$ where

$$
{b}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{b}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}-9 \\ 7 \\ 3\end{aligned}].
$$

If $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]$ then what is the value of ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
questions.worked_solution:
We need to find ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ such that 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{b}_{1}+{x}_{2}{b}_{2} & =x \\ {x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-9 \\ 7 \\ 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The equation above gives the system with the augmented matrix

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}2 & -3 & -9 \\ -1 & 2 & 7 \\ 1 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

Row-reducing the matrix using Gaussian elimination, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -3 & -9 \\ -1 & 2 & 7 \\ 1 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 3 \\ -1 & 2 & 7 \\ 2 & -3 & -9\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 2 & 10 \\ 2 & -3 & -9\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 2 & 10 \\ 0 & -3 & -15\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+\frac{3}{2}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 2 & 10 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}=3 \\ 2{x}_{2}=10.\end{aligned}
$$

From the second equation, we get ${x}_{2}=5.$ 

Therefore, $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 5\end{aligned}].$

Finally, ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=3+5=8.$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Coordinates of a Vector Relative To a Given Basis Containing Two Vectors
questions.problem:
Find the coordinates of the vector $x$ relative to the basis $B={{b}_{1},{b}_{2}},$ where

$$
{b}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -5\end{aligned}],\,{b}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 41\end{aligned}].
$$

If $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]$ then what is the value of ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
questions.worked_solution:
We need to find ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ such that 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{b}_{1}+{x}_{2}{b}_{2} & =x \\ {x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -5\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 2\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 41\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The equation above gives the system with the augmented matrix

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & -3 \\ -5 & 2 & 41\end{aligned}].
$$

Row-reducing the matrix using Gaussian elimination, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & -3 \\ -5 & 2 & 41\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+5{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & -3 \\ 0 & -13 & 26\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2}=-3 \\ -13{x}_{2}=26.\end{aligned}
$$

From the second equation, we get ${x}_{2}=-2.$ Substituting this into the first equation, we obtain

$$
{x}_{1}-3(-2)=-3\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=-9.
$$

Therefore, $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}-9 \\ -2\end{aligned}].$

Finally, ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=(-9)+(-2)=-11.$

questions.problem:
Find the coordinates of the vector $x$ relative to the basis $B={{b}_{1},{b}_{2}},$ where

$$
{b}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2\end{aligned}],\,{b}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 6\end{aligned}].
$$

If $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]$ then what is the value of ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
questions.worked_solution:
We need to find ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ such that 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{b}_{1}+{x}_{2}{b}_{2} & =x \\ {x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 6\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The equation above gives the system with the augmented matrix

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 2 \\ -2 & 1 & 6\end{aligned}].
$$

Row-reducing the matrix using Gaussian elimination, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 2 \\ -2 & 1 & 6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & 5 & 10\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}=2 \\ 5{x}_{2}=10.\end{aligned}
$$

From the second equation, we get ${x}_{2}=2.$ Substituting this into the first equation, we obtain

$$
{x}_{1}+2(2)=2\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=-2.
$$

Therefore, $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$

Finally, ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=(-2)+2=0.$

questions.problem:
Find the coordinates of the vector $x$ relative to the basis $B={{b}_{1},{b}_{2}},$ where

$$
{b}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{b}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 5 \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$

If $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]$ then what is the value of ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
questions.worked_solution:
We need to find ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ such that 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{b}_{1}+{x}_{2}{b}_{2} & =x \\ {x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 5 \\ 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The equation above gives the system with the augmented matrix

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 1 \\ 2 & 1 & 5 \\ 1 & 2 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we reduce $M$ using Gaussian elimination:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 1 \\ 2 & 1 & 5 \\ 1 & 2 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & -3 & 3 \\ 1 & 2 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & -3 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}=1 \\ -3{x}_{2}=3 \\ 0=1,\end{aligned}
$$

where the third equation is always false. Therefore, the system has no solution and we conclude that $x\notin \text{Span}{{b}_{1},{b}_{2}}.$

$$
{b}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -5 \\ 6\end{aligned}],\,{b}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -2 \\ 4\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -4 \\ 5\end{aligned}].
$$

If $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]$ then what is the value of ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
questions.worked_solution:
We need to find ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ such that  

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{b}_{1}+{x}_{2}{b}_{2} & =x \\ {x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -5 \\ 6\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -2 \\ 4\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -4 \\ 5\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The equation above gives the system with the augmented matrix

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 & 2 \\ -5 & -2 & -4 \\ 6 & 4 & 5\end{aligned}].
$$

Row-reducing the matrix using Gaussian elimination, we obtain the following: 

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 & 2 \\ -5 & -2 & -4 \\ 6 & 4 & 5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+\frac{5}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 & 2 \\ 0 & 8 & 1 \\ 6 & 4 & 5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 & 2 \\ 0 & 8 & 1 \\ 0 & -8 & -1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 & 2 \\ 0 & 8 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

 

The system is now 

$$
{\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2}=2 \\ 8{x}_{2}=1.\end{aligned}
$$

From the second equation, we get ${x}_{2}=\frac{1}{8}.$ Substituting this into the first equation, we obtain

$$
2{x}_{1}+4\cdot \frac{1}{8}=2\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=\frac{3}{4}.
$$

Therefore, $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{4} \\ \frac{1}{8}\end{aligned}].$ 

Finally, ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=\frac{3}{4}+\frac{1}{8}=\frac{7}{8}.$

{b}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 5\end{aligned}],\,{b}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,{b}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ 4\end{aligned}].
$$

If $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]$ then what is the value of ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}?$
questions.worked_solution:
We need to find ${x}_{1}$,  ${x}_{2}$, and ${x}_{3}$ such that  

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{b}_{1}+{x}_{2}{b}_{2}+{x}_{3}{b}_{3} & =x \\ {x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 5\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3 \\ -1\end{aligned}]+{x}_{3}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ 4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

From this, we get the system with the augmented matrix $M$, which we reduce using Gaussian elimination: 

$$
\begin{aligned}M= & [\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -1 & 1 \\ 2 & 3 & 1 & -2 \\ 5 & -1 & 2 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & -4 \\ 5 & -1 & 2 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-5){R}_{1} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & -4 \\ 0 & -6 & 7 & -1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+6{R}_{2} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & -4 \\ 0 & 0 & 25 & -25\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

  

The system is now 

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}-{x}_{3}=1 \\ {x}_{2}+3{x}_{3}=-4 \\ 25{x}_{3}=-25.\end{aligned}
$$

From the third equation, we get ${x}_{3}=-1.$ Substituting this into the second   equation yields

$$
{x}_{2}+3(-1)=-4\,⟹\,{x}_{2}=-1.
$$

 Finally,  by substituting ${x}_{2}=-1$ and ${x}_{3}=-1$ into the first equation we obtain

$$
{x}_{1}+(-1)-(-1)=1\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=1.
$$

Therefore, $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ -1\end{aligned}].$

So, we have 

$$
{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=1+(-1)+(-1)=-1.
$$

questions.problem:
Find the coordinates of the vector $x$ relative to the basis $B={{b}_{1},{b}_{2},{b}_{3}},$ where

$$
{b}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{b}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{b}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3 \\ -1\end{aligned}].
$$

If $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]$ then what is the value of ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}?$
questions.worked_solution:
We need to find ${x}_{1}$,  ${x}_{2}$, and ${x}_{3}$ such that 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{b}_{1}+{x}_{2}{b}_{2}+{x}_{3}{b}_{3} & =x \\ {x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+{x}_{3}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3 \\ -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

From this, we get the system with the augmented matrix $M$, which we reduce using Gaussian elimination:

$$
\begin{aligned}M= & [\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 2 & 2 \\ 1 & 2 & 1 & 3 \\ 1 & 1 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{1} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-1){R}_{1} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 & -2 & -3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & ↔{R}_{3} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & -1 & -2 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}+2{x}_{3}=2 \\ -{x}_{2}-2{x}_{3}=-3 \\ -{x}_{3}=1.\end{aligned}
$$

From third equation we get ${x}_{3}=-1$ and substituting this value into the second equation yields ${x}_{2}=-2(-1)+3=5.$ Finally, substituting ${x}_{2}=5$ and ${x}_{3}=-1$ into the first equation, we obtain

$$
{x}_{1}+2(5)+2(-1)=2\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=-6.
$$

Therefore, $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}-6 \\ 5 \\ -1\end{aligned}].$

Finally, 

$$
{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=(-6)+5+(-1)=-2.
$$

$$

$$

If $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]$ then what is the value of ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}?$
questions.worked_solution:
We need to find ${x}_{1}$,  ${x}_{2}$, and ${x}_{3}$ such that 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{b}_{1}+{x}_{2}{b}_{2}+{x}_{3}{b}_{3} & =x \\ {x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+{x}_{3}[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 2 \\ 0 \\ -8\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 8 \\ 5 \\ 4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

From this, we get the system with the augmented matrix $M$, which we reduce using Gaussian elimination:

$$
\begin{aligned}M= & [\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -3 & -3 \\ 1 & -1 & 2 & 8 \\ 1 & -2 & 0 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & -8 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{1} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -3 & -3 \\ 0 & -1 & 5 & 11 \\ 1 & -2 & 0 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & -8 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-1){R}_{1} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -3 & -3 \\ 0 & -1 & 5 & 11 \\ 0 & -2 & 3 & 8 \\ 0 & 1 & -8 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-2){R}_{2} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -3 & -3 \\ 0 & -1 & 5 & 11 \\ 0 & 0 & -7 & -14 \\ 0 & 1 & -8 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{4} & :={R}_{4}+{R}_{2} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -3 & -3 \\ 0 & -1 & -5 & 11 \\ 0 & 0 & -7 & -14 \\ 0 & 0 & -3 & 15\end{aligned}] & {R}_{4} & :={R}_{4}+(-\frac{3}{7}){R}_{2} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -3 & -3 \\ 0 & -1 & -5 & 11 \\ 0 & 0 & -7 & -14 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 21\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

 
The system is now 

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2}=-3 \\ -{x}_{2}+5{x}_{3}=11 \\ 13{x}_{3}=-14 \\ 0=21,\end{aligned}
$$

where the fourth equation is always false. Therefore, the system has no solution and we conclude that 

$$
x\notin \text{Span}{{b}_{1},{b}_{2},{b}_{3}}.
$$

questions.problem:
Find the coordinates of the vector $x$ relative to the basis $B={{b}_{1},{b}_{2},{b}_{3}},$ where

$$
{b}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -3 \\ 6 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,{b}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 0 \\ 10 \\ 10\end{aligned}],\,{b}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ -2 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}10 \\ -5 \\ 16 \\ 10\end{aligned}].
$$

If $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]$ then what is the value of ${x}_{1}?$
questions.worked_solution:
We need to find ${x}_{1}$,  ${x}_{2}$, and ${x}_{3}$ such that 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{b}_{1}+{x}_{2}{b}_{2}+{x}_{3}{b}_{3} & =x \\ {x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -3 \\ 6 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 0 \\ 10 \\ 10\end{aligned}]+{x}_{3}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ -2 \\ 0\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}10 \\ -5 \\ 16 \\ 10\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

From this, we get the system with the augmented matrix $M$, which we reduce using Gaussian elimination: 

$$
\begin{aligned}M= & [\begin{aligned}3 & 5 & 0 & 10 \\ -3 & 0 & 0 & -5 \\ 6 & 10 & -2 & 16 \\ 0 & 10 & 0 & 10\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+{R}_{1} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}3 & 5 & 0 & 10 \\ 0 & 5 & 0 & 5 \\ 6 & 10 & -2 & 16 \\ 0 & 10 & 0 & 10\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-2){R}_{1} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}3 & 5 & 0 & 10 \\ 0 & 5 & 0 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & -4 \\ 0 & 10 & 0 & 10\end{aligned}] & {R}_{4} & :={R}_{4}+(-2){R}_{2} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}3 & 5 & 0 & 10 \\ 0 & 5 & 0 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & -4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

   

The system is now 

$$
{\begin{aligned}3{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2}=10 \\ 5{x}_{2}=5 \\ -2{x}_{3}=-4 \\ 0=0,\end{aligned}
$$

From the fourth equation, we get a true statement. Then, from the second and third equation, we get ${x}_{2}=1$ and  ${x}_{3}=2$ respectively. Substituting ${x}_{2}=1$ into the first equation, we get 

$$
3{x}_{1}+5(1)=10\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=\frac{5}{3}.
$$

Therefore, $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}\frac{5}{3} \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$ 

Finally, ${x}_{1}=\frac{5}{3}.$

questions.problem:
Find the coordinates of the vector $x$ relative to the basis $B={{b}_{1},{b}_{2},{b}_{3}},$ where

$$
{b}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ 4\end{aligned}],\,{b}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3 \\ -2\end{aligned}],\,{b}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -2 \\ -4\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}7 \\ -15 \\ 6\end{aligned}].
$$

If $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]$ then what is the value of ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}?$
questions.worked_solution:
We need to find ${x}_{1}$,  ${x}_{2}$, and ${x}_{3}$ such that 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{b}_{1}+{x}_{2}{b}_{2}+{x}_{3}{b}_{3} & =x \\ {x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ 4\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3 \\ -2\end{aligned}]+{x}_{3}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -2 \\ -4\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}7 \\ -15 \\ 6\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

From this, we get the system with the augmented matrix $M$, which we reduce using Gaussian elimination:

$$
\begin{aligned}M= & [\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 0 & 7 \\ -2 & -3 & -2 & -15 \\ 4 & -2 & -4 & 6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 0 & 7 \\ 0 & -1 & -2 & -1 \\ 4 & -2 & -4 & 6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-4){R}_{1} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 0 & 7 \\ 0 & -1 & -2 & -1 \\ 0 & -6 & -4 & -22\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-6){R}_{2} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 0 & 7 \\ 0 & -1 & -2 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 8 & -16\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=7 \\ -{x}_{2}-2{x}_{3}=-1 \\ 8{x}_{3}=-16.\end{aligned}
$$

From third equation we get ${x}_{3}=-2$ and substituting this value into the second equation yields ${x}_{2}=-2(-2)+1=5.$ Finally, substituting ${x}_{2}=5$ into the first equation, we obtain

$$
{x}_{1}+5=7\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=2.
$$

Therefore, $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 5 \\ -2\end{aligned}].$

Finally, 

$$
{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=2+5+(-2)=5.
$$

Row-reducing the matrix using Gaussian elimination, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & -5 \\ 3 & 5 & -11 \\ 4 & 0 & -8\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & -5 \\ 0 & -4 & 4 \\ 4 & 0 & -8\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-4){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & -5 \\ 0 & -4 & 4 \\ 0 & -12 & 12\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-3){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & -5 \\ 0 & -4 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}

The augmented matrix above corresponds to the following system of equations: 

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}=-5 \\ -4{x}_{2}=4\end{aligned}

From the second equation, we get $x_2 =-1.$ Substituting this into the first equation, we obtain

$$
x_1 + 3 \left( -1 \right)  = -5
\qquad \Longrightarrow \qquad
x_1 = -2.

Therefore, ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14065173/assets/5e92e3cfdbf8d1c81be5b47124df9992d98835668154a50ece28cce8941860ca.png)

canonical_examples.problem:
Find the coordinates of the vector $\mathbf{x}$ relative to the basis $\mathcal{B}=\{ \mathbf{b}_1, \mathbf{b}_2, \mathbf{b}_3 \},$ where
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14065173/assets/4eb4b3533453f1a2c08c98bb8e6fd63e3f93563a4a2d56ecc0c0caef225b82e3.png)
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
We need to find $x_1,$ $x_2,$ and $x_3$ such that 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{b}_{1}+{x}_{2}{b}_{2}+{x}_{3}{b}_{3} & =x \\ {x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -9 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{3}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 7 \\ 6\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Writing the above system as an augmented matrix $M$ and reducing using Gaussian elimination, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & -9 & -1 & 7 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 & 6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & -9 & -1 & 7 \\ 0 & -3 & 1 & 5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-\frac{1}{3}){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & -9 & -1 & 7 \\ 0 & 0 & \frac{4}{3} & \frac{8}{3}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}=1 \\ -9{x}_{2}-{x}_{3}=7 \\ \frac{4}{3}{x}_{3}=\frac{8}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

From the third equation, we get $x_3 =2.$ Substituting this into the second equation, we obtain

$$
-9x_2 - 2 = 7 \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad x_2 = -1,
$$

and substituting $x_2=-1$ into the first equation, we get

$$
x_1+3(-1) = 1 \qquad\Longrightarrow\quad x_1 = 4.
$$

Therefore, ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14065173/assets/61d8401f40152a8eaeb30d3dc55d9548cac508b6239a9a70e99fbed9e271805b.png)
